page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a 4-core, 8-thread Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, the instance provides 8 burstable vCPUs backed by 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-BF16 for matrix operations. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance does not include local ephemeral storage and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2055.0, gzip compression reaching 33.32 GB/sec, and bzip3 single-threaded decompression achieving 13.87 GB/sec, all within the top 25th percentile. Multi-core operations align with the middle tier, producing a multi-core Geekbench score of 7957.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12373.16. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks sustains 52.11 GB/sec read and 50.44 GB/sec write speeds, though synthetic memory benchmarking via PassMark ranked in the lower quartile. The burstable CPU allocation profile supports variable computational spikes, but sustained heavy throughput may be bounded by CPU credit mechanisms.

Without local NVMe drives and lacking discrete GPUs, the instance relies on external block storage over the network. The flex tier provides a resource-dense configuration for compute tasks that do not demand non-stop 100% vCPU utilization. It is technically appropriate for web serving, continuous integration builds, application backends, and moderate batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor delivering 8 burstable vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 3.2 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory and 105 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 and AMX for advanced mathematical operations. The server provides a 2 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance testing demonstrates strong single-threaded results in Geekbench and compression utilities, while multi-core metrics like PassMark CPU remain in the median distribution. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, this instance suits bursty compute tasks, application servers, build systems, and web services that do not require continuous full-core utilization.
